title: How High Do Interest Rates Go? When Do Oil Prices Fall? Economist Answers | Peter Berezin
speaker: Peter Berezin (BCA Research)

macro_themes.view: Brent above $100 with high shipping costs and crack spreads; little scope for oil relief this year, probably improving next year.
A 'kinetic equilibrium' that will likely keep simmering for at least the next few months.
Higher yields are driven more by the AI capex boom crowding out other spending than by oil; 5.5% on the 10y is where he turns bullish on bonds.
Capex boom likely continues 12-24 months, peaking ~2028; stocks typically peak before capex, maybe in 2027.
The bubble is in earnings/margins rather than P/E; at 2019 margins the S&P forward P/E would be 27, not 19.
Real disposable income barely growing; consumption driven by wealthy households, so an AI/tech bust would hit spending hard with limited policy room.
Expects a bull market in reproductive tech (IVF) over the next 3-5 years as governments subsidise fertility.

calls.reason: Base case: stocks move sideways for rest of year then start falling next year, as stocks historically peak before the AI capex peak (~2028); recommends benchmark equity allocation.
calls.quote: I see stocks as likely moving sideways for the remainder of the year before starting to fall next year.

calls.condition: If the 10y reaches ~5.5% he would go long the 10-year (bullish bonds = bearish yields); relief for yields could come in 2027 if oil falls and AI capex busts.
calls.reason: AI capex and lower savings push rates up; at 5.5% the 10y locks in a good return so he'd buy bonds, possibly within a couple of weeks.
calls.quote: five and a half is the level on the 10 year that I've been saying that would be high enough for me to get bullish on bonds.

calls.reason: High shipping costs, crack spreads and Ukraine strikes on Russian refineries keep prices high; no big relief this year, probably improving next year.
calls.quote: I don't see a huge scope for relief in oil prices this year. Next year, who knows what'll happen. Probably things will improve by then.

notes: Host says 'happy Canadian Thanksgiving' (Oct 12, 2026), so recording may be ~Oct 12-13; listing date used. Brent quoted 'above $100'; 10y quoted '5.2 5.3%' (price_at_call 5.25 midpoint). TNX medium-term 'bullish' means yields may rise to 5.5 before he buys bonds; long-term bearish yields is implied by his 2027 relief scenario. Fed described as having just raised rates.
